section: Women's participation in the national movement in Andhra - Durgabai Deshmukh, Unnava Lakshmibayamma, Duvvuri Subbamma

accepted.s: The significance of Mahatma Gandhi’s 1921 coastal tour covering Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Chirala and Nellore was that it:
o: launched the Quit India Movement in coastal Andhra
resulted in the formation of the first provincial Congress ministry in Andhra
led to the immediate abolition of the zamindari system in Andhra
drew women into the national struggle in Andhra
accepted.x: Gandhi’s 1921 coastal tour in Andhra played an important role in drawing women into the national movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the central significance of the event rather than being distracted by later movements or reforms.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Amendment Bill, 2026:
1. Pawan Kalyan named Durgabai Deshmukh among the founding mothers of the Constitution.
2. The Bill provides for 33 per cent reservation.
3. The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha.
4. The reference was reported on 17 April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: Pawan Kalyan referred to Durgabai Deshmukh as a founding mother of the Constitution while welcoming the Bill, which concerns 33 per cent reservation and was introduced in the Lok Sabha; the report was dated 17 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the person, reservation figure, House and date before selecting the complete combination.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Annie Besant and Sarojini Naidu in relation to the Indian National Congress?
o: Annie Besant was the first Indian woman INC president in 1925, while Sarojini Naidu became the first woman INC president in 1917.
Annie Besant was the first woman INC president in 1917, while Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman INC president in 1925.
Annie Besant and Sarojini Naidu jointly became the first women INC presidents in 1925.
Sarojini Naidu was the first woman INC president in 1917, while Annie Besant was the first Indian woman INC president in 1925.
accepted.x: Annie Besant was the first woman president of the INC in 1917. Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman to preside over the INC, in 1925.
accepted.tq: Separate the broader category of first woman from the narrower qualification of first Indian woman.
